l4_steps.name: Evaluate OTA partnership opportunities
l4_steps.input: Market share data, OTA volume reports, channel performance benchmarks
l4_steps.output: OTA partnership shortlist with commercial rationale
l4_steps.kpi: OTA channel revenue contribution ≥25% of total passenger revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA market consolidation (Expedia/Booking.com duopoly) limits airline negotiating leverage on commission rates and parity terms

l4_steps.name: Negotiate OTA commercial agreement terms
l4_steps.input: OTA partnership shortlist, competitive commission benchmarks, IATA Resolution 818g standards
l4_steps.output: Draft commercial term sheet (commission rate, override tiers, content parity requirements)
l4_steps.kpi: Commission rate negotiated ≤12% of ticket value; override incentive thresholds agreed within 45 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OTAs demand last-look pricing rights and rate parity clauses that directly conflict with airline direct channel strategy and dynamic pricing

l4_steps.name: Execute OTA distribution agreement
l4_steps.input: Negotiated term sheet, legal review checklist, EU Package Travel Directive and US DOT transparency requirements
l4_steps.output: Signed OTA distribution agreement with SLA annexures
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution cycle ≤45 days from term sheet agreement
l4_steps.pain_point: Jurisdictional complexity across markets (EU Package Travel Directive 2015/2302, US DOT full-fare advertising rule 14 CFR Part 399) extends legal review and requires market-specific agreement variants

l4_steps.name: Configure OTA technical connectivity
l4_steps.input: Signed agreement, OTA technical specifications (IATA NDC Level 4 or GDS EDIFACT)
l4_steps.output: Validated API or GDS connection in test environment; go-live approval
l4_steps.kpi: API connectivity test pass rate 100% before go-live; integration delivery ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA NDC adoption remains below 40% industry-wide; most connections still use legacy GDS EDIFACT, limiting ancillary upsell capability and real-time inventory access

l4_steps.name: File fares and fare rules to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Approved fare structure, seasonal pricing calendar, OTA-specific fare product requirements
l4_steps.output: Published fares and fare rules in ATPCO database distributed to GDS channels
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing lead time ≥72h before sale date per ATPCO SOTI schedule; filing error rate ≤0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing windows create pricing latency vs. direct channel dynamic pricing; competitors using NDC bypass ATPCO for OTA-specific private offers, gaining speed-to-market advantage

l4_steps.name: Configure OTA channel fare availability in PSS
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM)
l4_steps.input: Published ATPCO fares, RM inventory allocation decisions, OTA booking class mapping
l4_steps.output: OTA booking class availability configured and active in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Fare availability accuracy ≥99.5% vs. ATPCO published fares; inventory update latency ≤15 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa inventory caching can lag up to 15 minutes on high-demand routes during peak booking windows, causing OTA booking failures, GDS error messages, and lost revenue on price-sensitive leisure routes

l4_steps.name: Distribute ancillary content to OTA channels
l4_steps.input: Ancillary product catalogue (bags, seats, meals, lounge), OTA NDC capability certification status
l4_steps.output: Structured ancillary offers available on OTA storefront for NDC-connected partners
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attach rate via OTA ≥18% of bookings; NDC ancillary revenue per booking ≥$22
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-NDC OTAs cannot render structured ancillary offers; EDIFACT-connected OTAs display ancillaries as free-text remarks only, reducing attach rate to <5% and suppressing ancillary revenue on high-volume OTA channels

l4_steps.name: Monitor OTA content parity compliance
l4_steps.input: Live OTA storefront pricing scraped across 50+ routes, direct channel published fares
l4_steps.output: Content parity compliance report; violation alerts triggered for OTA account management
l4_steps.kpi: Price parity violations ≤0.5% of sampled OTA fares per weekly audit cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: OTAs apply opaque loyalty discounts, packaging, and credit card rewards to undercut direct channel pricing, remaining technically parity-compliant while effectively bypassing parity agreements and eroding direct channel value proposition

l4_steps.name: Process OTA-originated bookings in PSS
l4_steps.input: OTA booking request via GDS sell message or NDC OrderCreate API
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PNR with OTA agency IATA number and pseudo-city code tagged
l4_steps.kpi: OTA booking acceptance rate ≥99.8%; booking confirmation latency ≤3 seconds via GDS, ≤1.5 seconds via NDC
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS booking surcharge of $3–$7 per segment raises airline cost of distribution vs. direct channel; carriers absorb cost to maintain OTA relationship but margin erodes on low-yield leisure itineraries

l4_steps.name: Validate OTA ticket issuance and EMD generation
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / IATA BSP Link
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR, OTA ticketing time limit, ancillary EMD requirements
l4_steps.output: Issued e-ticket (ET) and Electronic Miscellaneous Documents (EMDs) for all ancillary charges
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket issuance within BSP ticketing time limit 100%; EMD issuance error rate ≤0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA back-office systems frequently breach ticketing time limits due to payment processing delays, triggering automatic PNR cancellation in Altéa without customer notification — generating rebooking costs, customer complaints, and CSAT impact

l4_steps.name: Handle OTA booking modifications and cancellations
l4_steps.input: OTA-submitted modification or cancellation request via GDS or NDC OrderChange API
l4_steps.output: Updated or cancelled PNR; refund amount or credit voucher calculated and confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: OTA modification fulfilment rate ≥98%; refund processing ≤5 business days per IATA Resolution 824
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-NDC OTAs cannot submit structured order changes via API; refund workflows are manual when OTA uses EDIFACT, creating backlogs of 10,000+ cases during irregular operations (IROPS) events such as severe weather or ATC strikes

l4_steps.name: Reconcile OTA bookings against flown revenue
l4_steps.input: BSP/ARC settlement files, Amadeus Altéa PNR extract, OTA monthly booking reports
l4_steps.output: Revenue recognition journal entries; OTA revenue reconciliation report with variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completion within 3 business days of month close; revenue variance ≤0.1% of OTA channel revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA booking data arrives in multiple formats — BSP XML, ARC ACH files, and direct NDC API logs — requiring manual transformation and mapping before SAP ingestion, extending the month-close cycle by 1–2 days

l4_steps.name: Process BSP/ARC settlement for OTA bookings
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation)
l4_steps.input: Validated OTA sales data, BSP billing memoranda, ARC weekly transaction reports
l4_steps.output: Settled BSP payment received; ARC remittance filed and confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: BSP settlement on-time rate 100%; settlement discrepancy rate ≤0.05% of billed amount
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA agents with multiple IATA numbers split bookings across sub-entities to stay below BSP credit limits, creating reconciliation gaps, default risk exposure, and triggering IATA credit management review processes

l4_steps.name: Audit and pay OTA commission and override incentives
l4_steps.input: OTA quarterly sales performance report, commission rate schedule, override tier thresholds from contract
l4_steps.output: Commission payment instruction processed; override incentive credit note issued
l4_steps.kpi: Commission payment accuracy ≥99.9%; override incentive payment within 30 days of quarter close
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual commission calculation for multi-tier OTA override structures (base + volume override + market development funds) is error-prone; disputes with large OTAs (Expedia, Booking.com) over override eligibility can delay payments 60+ days and damage commercial relationships

l4_steps.name: Analyse OTA channel performance vs. targets
l4_steps.input: OTA booking volumes, revenue by route, ancillary attach rates, cost-of-sale per ticket by channel
l4_steps.output: OTA channel performance dashboard; monthly KPI scorecard distributed to VP Distribution
l4_steps.kpi: OTA revenue contribution vs. plan ±5%; cost of distribution per ticket ≤$15 including GDS fees and commissions
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA data-sharing agreements vary significantly — major OTAs withhold passenger-level booking data citing GDPR and commercial confidentiality, preventing complete channel profitability analysis and obscuring true margin contribution by OTA partner

l4_steps.name: Review OTA contract performance and renewal decision
l4_steps.input: OTA channel KPI scorecard, contracted volume commitments, competitive distribution benchmarks
l4_steps.output: OTA contract renewal recommendation; renegotiation mandate or termination notice issued ≥90 days before expiry
l4_steps.kpi: OTA contracts reviewed annually; renewal or renegotiation decision finalised ≥90 days before expiry date
l4_steps.pain_point: Bilateral OTA contracts frequently lack performance clawback provisions; underperforming OTAs retain preferred commission rates and override eligibility without meeting volume commitments, reducing airline's ability to redirect inventory to higher-yield channels
